problems.explain: Write 15° as 45° − 30°, and tan(α ± β) = (tan α ± tan β)/(1 ∓ tan α tan β). With 1 and √3/3 that simplifies, after multiplying top and bottom by the conjugate, to 2 − √3. (tan(α + β) is not tan α + tan β.) So tan 15° = 2 − √3.

prompt.v: Which of these is equal to tan 2θ?

problems.text: trig simplify: tan(2*t); options a: tan(t)/(1 - tan(t)^2) | b: (2*cot(t))/(1 - cot(t)^2) | c: cot(t)/(1 - cot(t)^2) | d: (2*tan(t))/(1 - tan(t)^2)
problems.explain: tan 2θ = tan(θ + θ) = (tan θ + tan θ)/(1 − tan θ tan θ). (The bottom is 1 − tan²θ; with 1 + tan²θ it is sin 2θ instead.) So (2 tan θ)/(1 − tan²θ).

problems.explain: tan θ/sin θ = (sin θ/cos θ) ÷ sin θ = 1/cos θ = sec θ. (The sines cancel and leave 1 over cosine.) So sec θ.
